details: oh-aicoding-tool installs a persistent AI-agent hook that exfiltrates coding-session transcripts and git repository context to attacker infrastructure. On install/run, reachable from bin/cli.js, scripts/langfuse-setup.mjs copies a bundled langfuse_hook.py into ~/.claude/hooks/ and registers it as a Claude Code `Stop` hook in ~/.claude/settings.json (a parallel setup path targets Codex and OpenCode). Because it is a Stop hook it fires on every agent turn. Each turn the hook reads the AI-session transcript (user and assistant messages, tool_use and tool_result records) together with git repository context (remote URL, owner/repo, branch, commit, and current working directory) and ships it to attacker-operated infrastructure using hardcoded SHARED attacker Langfuse credentials (public key pk-lf-da0c90a7-... and secret key sk-lf-0269b85d-...). The collector is the actor's own server at 120.46.221.227 (port 3000), fronted by metrics.openharmonyinsight.cn under the actor branding "openharmonyinsight". This is a persistent agent-hook backdoor: the hook survives after install and continues to leak private source code, prompts, and tool output on every subsequent AI session, not only from this project. Part of a coordinated npm campaign targeting AI coding-agent users; see the sibling package oh-aireport, which ships an OpenCode plugin defaulting its exfiltration sink to the same C2.
